title: Deep events kept a 9.52-point larger-event share contrast after cell and magnitude-type matching in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether exact preferred moment-magnitude type mix accounts for a reported depth-size contrast. We used a fixed ComCat snapshot for 2000-2025. Fifteen cell-type groups in nine 20-degree cells retained 873 intermediate and 597 deep M5.5+ events. Fixed pooled weights gave an M6.5+ share of 18.79% at depths of at least 300 km and 9.27% at 70 to below 300 km. The difference was 9.52 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 4.45 to 14.74 points. On the same events, adding exact type weights to geographic weights changed the contrast by +0.16 points, with an interval of -1.28 to +2.75 points. Thus this matching did not remove the contrast. Eight planned checks retained positive joint contrasts. This extends prior campaign geographic matching on the same source, not an independent confirmation. Type selection, broad cells, changing methods, unknown completeness and conditional uncertainty prevent a causal depth claim. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Depth contrasts on the same retained sample, with planned checks. Bars show conditional 95% calendar-year block intervals. Primary target is M6.5+ among M5.5+ events.
